subject: ClinicAI — follow-up: ephemeral logs / tailored retention options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.g@clinicaid.com>, Alex Thompson <alex.t@clinicaid.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: ClinicAI — follow-up: ephemeral logs / tailored retention options

Hi Maya / Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of ask: ClinicAI needs to process PHI-adjacent records for feature enrichment but cannot allow any persistent PII in our standard logging. You asked about: a) 0-retention for PII, b) short-term logs for billing/audit, and c) EU residency for any stored artifacts.

2) Options we discussed (high-level):
   - Option A — Zero PII retention: strip PII before persist; transient KV/cache only in-memory; no persistent request logs containing identifiable fields.
   - Option B — Short-window logs: anonymized request logs persisted 24–72 hours for debugging and billing, then irreversibly deleted.
   - Option C — Mixed approach: PII never stored; system keeps minimal non-identifying telemetry for 90 days in EU region only (if required by audit) — negotiable.

3) Controls & evidence: we can provide SOC 2 artifacts, KMS key split options, and an exported sample retention schedule. For the EU residency ask, we will run inference in the EU region and ensure customer data is pinned to EU storage.

4) Next steps I propose:
   a) ClinicAI confirms which option (A/B/C) you want to pilot.
   b) Redwood drafts a short Data Retention Addendum (attached) with the chosen retention window and deletion proof expectations.
   c) PoC scope: 2-week trial on EU region with synthetic-sanitized records.

Please confirm who from legal (if anyone) should be looped in — Tim? Also any hard constraints on the minimum retention for billing or auditors would be helpful.

I'll follow up with a draft DAA and a mutual action plan.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ClinicAI — follow-up: ephemeral logs / tailored retention options

Thanks, Soojin — useful recap. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we pick an option: 

1) Billing and audit: our finance/audit team requires an immutable usage record for charge reconciliation for 6 months. Is there a way to reconcile without storing PII (we can accept hashed identifiers if salt is customer-controlled).

2) Deletion proof: for Option B (24–72h), we need evidence we performed deletion (deletion proofs or a signed retention report). Is Redwood able to provide a verifiable deletion artifact?

3) Tokenization: when you say stripping PII, are you doing deterministic tokenization that could be reversed if someone had access to a mapping table? We need assurances that PII is not reversible by Redwood or an operator.

Looping Tim from legal to confirm any contract-level requirements — Tim, are you able to review the attached DAA draft and comment on deletion proof language?

Best,
Maya
VP Product & Privacy
ClinicAI

Thanks Maya — answers inline below and next steps at the end.

> 1) Billing and audit: our finance/audit team requires an immutable usage record for charge reconciliation for 6 months. Is there a way to reconcile without storing PII (we can accept hashed identifiers if salt is customer-controlled).

Yes — we support customer-supplied hashing salts and also token-only billing records. We can emit an immutable usage ledger (billing-only) that contains only non-identifying IDs + aggregated token counts; ledger records can be exported and retained for 6 months in your EU tenant. No plaintext PII fields will be present.

> 2) Deletion proof: for Option B (24–72h), we need evidence we performed deletion (deletion proofs or a signed retention report). Is Redwood able to provide a verifiable deletion artifact?

Short answer: yes. We can provide periodically generated retention reports and cryptographic deletion receipts for persisted objects (hash of object + deletion timestamp signed by our key). We will include deletion-proof language in the DAA.

> 3) Tokenization: when you say stripping PII, are you doing deterministic tokenization that could be reversed if someone had access to a mapping table? We need assurances that PII is not reversible by Redwood or an operator.

We do not perform reversible deterministic tokenization by default. For strict non-reversibility we recommend client-side deterministic hashing with a customer-managed salt (recommended for compliance). If you need server-side hashing with no reversible mapping, we can enable one-way hashing and ensure mapping tables are not kept. We'll call this out in section 2 of the DAA.

Attachments: the "clinicai-data-retention-daa-draft.pdf" contains three draft clauses: zero-PII retention, short-window logs (24/72h), and EU residency assurances. I've also attached a simple redline spreadsheet that maps retention windows to product behaviors.

Proposed next steps: 
 - ClinicAI picks either Option A (zero-PII) or Option B (short-window).
 - Redwood to share an updated DAA with explicit deletion-proof mechanics and sample exported ledger format.
 - Run a 2-week PoC in EU region using synthetic data and customer-supplied salt for hashing.

If that all looks good I'll circulate a short mutual action plan and timeline.

Thanks,

--
